## Design

### 2026-10-12 – I started the design on the case, I made sure it would fit the pcb inside of it, I designed in an acrylic face so that the light can shine through, I made sure that there was room for the lights to be

**3h**

I started the design on the case, I made sure it would fit the pcb inside of it, I designed in an acrylic face so that the light can shine through, I made sure that there was room for the lights to be spaced away from the acrylic to naturally diffuse the light as opposed to having sharp dots, I then added a stand to make the clock stand up, and I added numbers around the face so that you can read it.

### 2026-10-14 – Added in a hole for the usb c cable to go through so that it can connect to the usb c port on the board, this allows the clock to recieve power and ultimately function, otherwise, there would be no wa

**1h**

Added in a hole for the usb c cable to go through so that it can connect to the usb c port on the board, this allows the clock to recieve power and ultimately function, otherwise, there would be no way to get a usb c cable into the case and it would be impossible to power the clock

### 2026-10-15 – I played around with different tools, trying to find a good way to allow light to sneak out around the edges of the clock, illuminating the surrounding walls with what hopefully turns out to be a cool

**3h**

I played around with different tools, trying to find a good way to allow light to sneak out around the edges of the clock, illuminating the surrounding walls with what hopefully turns out to be a cool pattern, I think it will be based off of how it looks in cad, but I guess I won't know until its built, this should also improve airflow to the internals, helping them stay cool while they work hard, the strategy I settled on using was to create the shapes in a sketch, then deboss them through the case, I spent a while trying to get it to copy the deboss all the way around, but then I remembered that circular patterns exist, so I ended up just doing that instead.
